items.title: Fosun Files for ClubMed IPO in Hong Kong
items.summary: ClubMed's revenue rose less than 2% last year, suggesting that "premiumization" isn't delivering pricing power yet. An IPO would generate capital that might help fix that.

items.title: Marriott Presses Sales Teams on $1.55 Billion ‘Gap to Goal’ for 2027 Groups
items.summary: Marriott has given sales teams a year-end stretch goal of $1.55 billion for group bookings for next year at the hotels it manages in the U.S. and Canada. Its global 2027 group sales look "flattish." Other companies are more upbeat.

items.title: Your Hotel Is Hot on TikTok Go. But AI Got All The Facts Wrong.
items.summary: TikTok's new hotel and experience booking feature is supposed to connect travelers with real properties, but an abundance of AI-generated content has property owners concerned.

items.title: Choice Hotels Hands CEO Job to Insider as It Tries to Reverse a Slump Versus Rivals
items.summary: Choice moved Dominic Dragisich around various key leadership roles over nearly a decade to prepare him for the top job.

items.title: Africa’s Next Tourism Boom Will Be Won in the Mid-Market
items.summary: As travelers increasingly seek value without compromising on quality or experience, Africa’s biggest tourism opportunity may lie in building the reliable, professionally managed middle tier that much of the continent has historically lacked.

items.title: Airbnb Is Testing Lower Fees for Hosts Who Bring Their Own Guests
items.summary: Call it "direct booking" if you like, but the reservation still runs on Airbnb's platform. And Airbnb's take rate now seems variable.

items.title: How SingleThread Is Growing Without Copying Itself
items.summary: SingleThread is expanding thoughtfully, leaning on translating its service culture through people and giving them bigger challenges to tackle.

items.title: Canadians Were Just Starting to Come Around to U.S. Travel. Then Came the Trade War.
items.summary: Canadian travel to the U.S. had just hit its fourth straight month of year-over-year gains when tariff disputes between the two countries escalated — a worrisome development for hotel operators and destinations.
